items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Sam Morgan had a nice little group at the time. They were playing what they felt and what they knew.

ctx.x: Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. And I admired, because Dodds was way ahead of us in his ideas, in his playing. He was matured. And it was something that you didn't learn in the method. And even I'm from downtown, you see. You take Piku, you take Teyo, they played beautiful jazz but it was mostly of a classical thing. You know what I mean? Playing right and all like that. But they didn't play Gut Bucket like, or had a little Gut Bucket band uptown. Buddy Petit had one downtown because they used to buck each…
And when you started having lessons, you started to read straight away?
